metaDescription: Six Euhomy ice makers compared across clear cube, nugget, smart bullet and commercial under-counter models, with output, tank and noise differences explained.
expertTake: The Euhomy 45 lb clear cube maker is the pick for a household that wants slow-melting square cubes and a high daily output, while the Euhomy 44 lb nugget machine is the choice for chewable ice. The smart 26 lb bullet unit is the cheap, app-controlled starter. Skip the commercial unit unless you have a drain, because it is plumbing first and appliance second.
introParagraphs: One maker can sell four different kinds of ice machine under a single name, and they have little in common beyond the logo. A cube maker freezes square cubes in a tray, a bullet maker chills prongs, a nugget maker scrapes pellets off a cold cylinder and a commercial unit stores ice in an insulated bin.

Picking within a brand is therefore a question of the kind of ice, the daily volume and the room it has to live in. We compare the machines on how they make ice, how much they hold, how noisy they are and what they ask of you, and rank who each one suits.

products.name: Euhomy countertop ice cube maker, 45 lb per day, 24 clear cubes

specList.label: Water supply
specList.value: Manual fill or bottle, two ways

products.description:
Where bullet makers freeze ice around prongs, a cube maker freezes water in a tray, and that method produces square, crystal-clear cubes that melt slowly. This Euhomy makes 24 of them every 10 to 20 minutes and up to 45 pounds a day, a high output for a countertop machine.

Adjustable ice thickness lets you make thinner cubes for quick chilling or thicker ones for slow-sipping drinks. Two ways to add water, by manual fill or by a bottle with an opening under two inches, make it easy to place anywhere. A self-cleaning function covers the routine flush.

Against the nugget machines it makes harder, slower-melting ice with less noise, and it cannot make chewable pellets. Descale regularly, keep clearance around the vents and note that the cycle time varies with room and water temperature.
products.bestFor: Households that want clear, slow-melting cubes at high output.
pros: Up to 45 lb per day on a countertop
cons: Cycle time ranges from 10 to 20 minutes

products.name: Euhomy clear ice cube maker with 1.5L top tank, 34 lb, 16 cubes

specList.label: Water
specList.value: 1.5L top tank, up to 2L total with bottle

products.description:
A top tank means you pour water in from above without sliding the machine out, and this Euhomy pairs a 1.5 liter top tank with the option of a bottle to bring total capacity to about two liters. It makes 16 crystal-clear cubes per cycle in roughly 13 minutes, up to 34 pounds a day.

An LCD display shows indicators for clean and fill states, and adjustable multi-sized ice lets you choose cube thickness. The maker claims quieter running than earlier models. It makes less than the 45 lb unit and is a touch smaller, which suits a modest household.

Compared with the 45 lb model it is easier to fill and lighter on output. Keep the top clear of clutter, descale monthly in hard water and give it airflow on all sides.
products.bestFor: Smaller households that want clear cubes and easy top-filling.
pros: Top tank is easy to fill
cons: Lower output than the 45 lb model
13 minute cycle is slower than bullet units

products.name: Euhomy nugget ice maker countertop, 44 lb, 7 to 10 min, scoop included
products.description:
Nugget ice is made by an auger that scrapes a frozen cylinder and compresses the flakes into soft pellets, which explains why this Euhomy is heavier and louder than the cube maker. It delivers 44 pounds a day and the maker claims soft chewable ice in seven to ten minutes.

The pellets are airy and crunchy, and they soak up the flavor of whatever drink they sit in, which is why coffee and soda drinkers like them. A scoop and basket come in the box, and a self-cleaning cycle handles routine flushing. As with every nugget machine, scale on the cylinder is the main enemy.

Compared with the 45 lb cube maker it makes softer, faster-melting ice and more noise. Descale every month or two, keep the vents clear and drain it if it will sit idle.
products.bestFor: Chewable-ice fans with heavy daily use.
pros: 44 lb per day of soft nugget ice
cons: Louder and heavier than the cube maker
Scale slows the auger if ignored

products.name: Euhomy nugget ice maker countertop, 35 lb, 7 min, stainless steel
products.description:
This stainless version trades some output for a more durable-looking body. It produces up to 35 pounds a day, with a claimed seven minute first batch of the same soft nugget ice as the 44 lb model, and a self-cleaning function for routine flushes.

A stainless finish resists scratches and fingerprints better than a plastic shell and suits a kitchen with other steel appliances. It is a sonic-style nugget maker, so it carries the same auger noise and the same scale risk as the other nugget machines. The output is enough for a family without being large.

Compared with the 44 lb Euhomy it is smaller and a bit quicker to start. Descale monthly, wipe the bin and keep several inches of clearance for the compressor.
products.bestFor: Kitchens with stainless appliances that want nugget ice.
cons: Lower output than the 44 lb model
Nugget auger noise and scale risk

products.name: Euhomy smart bullet ice maker countertop, 26 lb, app and voice control
products.description:
The simplest machine in the range is the bullet maker, which chills metal prongs and lets ice grow around them. This smart version adds an app and voice control, so you can start ice from your phone before you walk into the kitchen. It produces nine cubes in as little as six minutes and 26 pounds a day.

Bullet cubes are hard and slower melting than nugget, a good fit for coolers and drinks, and the machine is lighter and cheaper than the cube and nugget units. The compromise is capacity and ice type: it cannot make chewable pellets and its output is the lowest here.

Against the cube maker it is faster per batch and smaller. Keep the vents clear, descale every month or two and dry the machine if it sits unused.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a cheap, app-controlled ice maker.
pros: Nine cubes in about six minutes
Lighter and cheaper than the other types
cons: Lowest output of the group at 26 lb

products.name: Euhomy commercial under-counter ice maker, 100 lb, 33 lb bin, ETL

specList.label: Certification
specList.value: ETL for commercial and home use

products.description:
This is the Euhomy that behaves like a built-in appliance: it makes up to 100 pounds a day at 45 cubes per cycle and stores 33 pounds in a bin under a counter. The maker highlights ETL certification for both commercial and home use.

It needs a water line and a drain, which makes installation a project that the countertop units avoid. The reward is a steady ice supply for a home bar, a basement or a small business, with a bin that holds the ice cold. At 33 pounds the bin is modest, so a party relies on continuous production.

Compared with the 45 lb countertop cube maker it makes more than twice as much and stores it. Set a routine for sanitizing the bin, brushing the condenser and descaling the water lines.
products.bestFor: Home bars and small businesses that want a plumbed ice supply.
pros: Up to 100 lb per day with a 33 lb bin
ETL certified for commercial and home use
cons: Needs a water line and a drain
33 lb bin runs out at a big party

buyingCriteria.explanation: Euhomy sells all three. The 45 lb and 34 lb cube makers freeze clear square cubes in a tray, the 26 lb bullet maker freezes prongs, and the 44 lb and 35 lb nugget makers scrape soft pellets off a cylinder. Cubes melt slowest, bullets are quick and cheap, and nuggets are chewable. Pick the ice first, because no machine can switch types. A household that buys a bullet maker and then discovers it wanted chewable nuggets will not be able to fix that with any setting, so decide before you click buy.

Output spans 26 pounds on the bullet unit to 100 on the commercial one, with cycle times from about 6 minutes for a bullet batch to 10 to 20 minutes for the cube maker. A higher daily rating helps most when guests are coming, but the cycle time decides how soon the first drink gets ice.

The 34 lb cube maker's top tank is easy to pour into, and the 45 lb cube maker offers manual fill or a bottle with an opening under two inches. Larger tanks mean fewer trips to the tap. Commercial units need a plumbed line and a drain, which is a larger commitment.

Cube and bullet makers are quieter than nugget machines, whose auger adds grinding to the compressor hum. Euhomy claims quieter running on its newer cube makers, but the figures are the maker's own. Place the machine on a solid counter with clearance and keep it away from a bedroom wall.

The smart bullet model offers app and voice control, and the cube makers have LCD displays with indicators. These conveniences help you schedule ice and read the machine's state. They add electronics, so a simple model has fewer parts to fail. A machine that cannot make ice without its app is a poor bargain, so confirm there is a panel button for basic operation before you count on the smart layer.

Every Euhomy listed here has a self-cleaning function, but none removes mineral scale. A monthly or bimonthly descale with citric acid is the real maintenance. The maker also advises running clean-water cycles after a deep clean and discarding the first ice.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ice type
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated cube, bullet, nugget and commercial makers and judged each against its own purpose. The cube maker led for slow-melting ice, the nugget machine for chewable. Mixed comparisons were avoided.

howWeEvaluated.title: Output and speed
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared 26 to 100 pounds per day and cycle times of about 6 to 20 minutes. We treated the figures as best-case ratings. Higher output scored for entertaining.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fill and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the top tank, bottle fill and bin size, plus the plumbing needs of the commercial unit. Easy filling scored higher. A 33 lb bin was noted as modest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise and features
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered nugget auger noise, the maker's quiet claims, LCD displays and app control. Simple designs scored for reliability. Smart features earned credit for convenience.

howWeEvaluated.title: Maintenance
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted self-cleaning cycles, the maker's descaling guidance and accessory content. None removes scale on its own. Clear instructions raised the score.

cards.label: Countertop
cards.text: The cube, nugget and bullet models need only an outlet and a manual fill. They are portable but hold little.

cards.label: Under-counter
cards.text: The commercial 100 lb unit makes and stores far more but needs a water line and a drain.

howToChoose.note: Countertop for flexibility; under-counter for a permanent bar.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: High daily output, a quick cycle, a big tank and an easy way to bag and freeze the ice.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The 45 lb cube maker and the 100 lb commercial unit lead on volume. The commercial unit also stores 33 pounds.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You use ice daily or entertain often. The 45 lb cube maker and the commercial unit repay in volume.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want ice a few times a week. The smart bullet unit does the job.

maintenance.why: Scale cuts output and slows the auger. Citric acid or a maker-approved descaler removes it.
Residue leaves a taste. The maker advises two or three clean cycles and discarding early ice.
A damp bin grows biofilm. A mild cleaner and a rinse keep it fresh, and a dry cloth afterward removes the film that standing water leaves behind in the corners.

maintenance.task: Sanitize and clean the condenser on the commercial unit
maintenance.why: Slime and dust shorten a commercial machine's life. Remove the ice before sanitizing, rinse thoroughly and run a cycle with the bin empty before putting the machine back into service.
Standing water grows slime. Drain and leave the lid open.

faq.q: What is the difference between Euhomy cube and bullet ice makers?
faq.a: Cube makers freeze water in a tray to make clear square cubes, while bullet makers freeze ice around prongs. Cubes are slower melting, and bullet makers are faster and smaller. A cube maker also tends to produce a larger, flatter piece, so a drink chills a little slower at first and stays cold much longer, which suits a tall glass or a cooler.

faq.q: Which Euhomy makes the most ice?
faq.a: The commercial under-counter unit claims 100 pounds a day, and the countertop cube maker claims 45. Output claims are best-case and fall in a warm room. For a party, count on the bin rather than the rating, since a 33 pound bin and a continuous 100 pound production line behave very differently at a peak hour than the daily total suggests.

faq.q: Do Euhomy ice makers need plumbing?
faq.a: The countertop models do not. They fill by hand, from a tank or a bottle. Only the commercial under-counter unit needs a water line and a drain.

Monthly is a safe rhythm for an Euhomy, stretching to two months in soft water. Scale cuts output and slows the auger. Self-cleaning cycles do not remove it. Look for white crust in the tank, cloudy cubes or a machine that cycles more slowly than it used to, and treat any of them as a reminder to descale.

faq.q: Is nugget ice worth the extra noise?
faq.a: For anyone who prefers chewable ice that soaks up the drink's flavor, the answer is yes. Nugget machines are heavier and louder than cube makers, so place them with that in mind. A kitchen counter away from the living room is ideal, and a rubber mat under the feet takes the buzz out of a hollow cabinet top.

The 45 lb and 34 lb cube makers accept a bottle with a narrow opening. Using filtered or bottled water reduces scale and keeps the ice cleaner. A bottle fill is also handy where the sink is far from the counter, though a wide-mouth jug will not fit, so check the opening against the maker's two inch limit before you buy bottles in bulk.
